summary: Both editions were independently checked against every clause of the selected Greek. They preserve the time and place links, spirit transport, worthiness and former-sins explanation, the woman’s identification and dialogue, complete letter-for-letter copying, inability to make out syllables, and sudden snatching by an unseen agent. The simplified edition’s sentence divisions and past-tense narration introduce no concrete fidelity defect. Both editions retain the working readings while disclosing alternatives consistently with the supplied project reports, distinguishing corrections, editorial emendation, explanatory commentary, and mediated Ethiopic evidence. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
